usageNotes: Use this to evacuate all (or a filtered set of) guests from the cluster to a single target node in one API call — common for scheduled maintenance or emergency node drain. The `online` flag enables live migration for VMs and restart migration for containers, minimizing downtime; omitting it causes VMs to be shut down before moving. Returns a worker UPID immediately; track progress via the tasks API, as the actual migrations run asynchronously.

examples.summary: Live-migrate all guests to node pve2, up to 4 concurrent workers

destructiveReason: Migrating all guests disrupts any VMs/CTs that cannot live-migrate (e.g., those using local disks without with-local-disks), causing a full shutdown-and-restart cycle and a service outage for those workloads.
tips: Use the `vms` parameter to limit the operation to specific VMIDs rather than migrating every guest on the cluster — safer for production environments.
Set `with-local-disks: true` only if the target node has sufficient storage and network bandwidth; live storage migration is significantly slower than shared-storage migration.
Prefer `max-workers` (not the deprecated `maxworkers`) and keep it low (2–4) to avoid saturating cluster network bandwidth during migration.
The caller needs VM.Migrate on '/' for a full cluster sweep; if scoping to specific VMIDs via `vms`, the permission can be scoped per VM instead.
